pages.title: What you will learn
pages.body:
> 📊 **Strand 4 — Handling Data**
Collecting, organising, presenting and interpreting information to make good decisions.

> 🎯 **Content standard** (B7.4.1)
- B7.4.1.2 — Determine the measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) for given ungrouped data and use them to solve problems.

> 🎯 **In this chapter you will learn to:**
- calculate the mean of a list of data and of data in a frequency table
- solve problems involving the mean (average), including finding a missing value
- find the median of a list of data (odd and even number of items) and of data in a frequency table

pages.title: The mean
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Calculate the mean for given ungrouped data and use it to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B7.4.1.2.1
> 🔑 **Key idea: Mean** — The **mean** (arithmetic average) of a set of data is the sum of all the items divided by the number of items: **Mean =** [[sum of items/number of items]].
## ✏️ Example 14.1
Find the mean of the data set {8, 9, 7, 6, 8, 10}.
**Solution**
Mean = [[8 + 9 + 7 + 6 + 8 + 10/6]] = [[48/6]] = **8**
## ✏️ Example 14.2
The marks obtained by 20 learners in a short class test (marked out of 10) are:
| 3 | 4 | 2 | 4 | 3 | 2 | 2 | 5 | 4 | 3 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1 | 2 | 6 | 3 | 5 | 5 | 2 | 4 | 1 |
Find the mean mark.
**Solution**
Sum = 3 + 4 + 2 + 4 + 3 + 2 + 2 + 5 + 4 + 3 + 4 + 1 + 2 + 6 + 3 + 5 + 5 + 2 + 4 + 1 = 65
Mean = [[65/20]] = **3.25**
## The mean of data in a frequency table
When data are in a frequency table, multiply each value (x) by its frequency (f), add the products, then divide by the total frequency:
Mean = [[sum of fx/sum of f]]
## ✏️ Example 14.3
Find the mean score of a class test (out of 5) given in the frequency table.
| **Score (x)** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency (f) | 2 | 6 | 4 | 5 | 3 |
**Solution**
| **Score (x)** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** | **Total** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency (f) | 2 | 6 | 4 | 5 | 3 | 20 |
| fx | 2 | 12 | 12 | 20 | 15 | 61 |
Mean = [[61/20]] = **3.05**

pages.title: Example 14.4
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 14.4
Find the mean age of children at a party.
| **Age (x)** | **1** | **3** | **5** | **6** | **7** | **8** | **9** | **10** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency (f) | 2 | 5 | 6 | 10 | 8 | 5 | 3 | 1 |
**Solution**
Σf = 2 + 5 + 6 + 10 + 8 + 5 + 3 + 1 = 40
Σfx = 2 + 15 + 30 + 60 + 56 + 40 + 27 + 10 = 240
Mean = [[240/40]] = **6 years**
## Problems on the mean
## ✏️ Example 14.5
A shopkeeper sold the following numbers of loaves of bread over 6 days: 25, 48, 25, 33, 57, 50. What was the average number of loaves sold each day?
**Solution**
Mean = [[25 + 48 + 25 + 33 + 57 + 50/6]] = [[238/6]] ≈ **39.7 loaves** (about 40 a day)
## ✏️ Example 14.6
Sena's scores in five subjects this term are 75, 87, 90, 88 and 79. What must she score in the sixth subject to have an average of 85?
**Solution**
Let the sixth score be x.
[[75 + 87 + 90 + 88 + 79 + x/6]] = 85
419 + x = 85 × 6 = 510
**x = 91**
Sena must score 91.
> 🎯 **BECE tip** For "missing value" problems: **total needed = mean × number of items**. Then subtract the total you already have.

pages.title: The median
pages.body:
> 🎯 **You will learn to:** Calculate the median for given ungrouped data and use it to solve problems.
Curriculum indicator B7.4.1.2.2
> 🔑 **Key idea: Median** — The **median** is the **middle value** when the data are arranged in order (an **array**). For n items: if n is odd, the median is the [[n + 1/2]]th item; if n is even, the median is the mean of the two middle items (the [[n/2]]th and the ([[n/2]] + 1)th).
## ✏️ Example 14.7
Find the median of a) 19, 29, 36, 15, 20 b) 8, 9, 7, 6, 8, 10
**Solution**
a) Array: 15, 19, **20**, 29, 36. There are 5 values (odd), so the median is the 3rd value: **20**.
b) Array: 6, 7, **8, 8**, 9, 10. There are 6 values (even), so the median is the mean of the 3rd and 4th values: [[8 + 8/2]] = **8**.
## ✏️ Example 14.8
Find the median mark for the class test in the frequency table.
| **Score** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 2 | 6 | 4 | 5 | 3 |
**Solution**
There are 20 values, so the median is the mean of the 10th and 11th values. Use **cumulative frequency** (a running total):
| **Score** | **1** | **2** | **3** | **4** | **5** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency | 2 | 6 | 4 | 5 | 3 |
| Cumulative frequency | 2 | 8 | 12 | 17 | 20 |
The 9th to 12th values are all 3, so the 10th and 11th values are both 3. **Median = 3**.

pages.title: Example 14.9
pages.body:
## ✏️ Example 14.9
Find the median age of children at a party.
| **Age (x)** | **1** | **3** | **5** | **6** | **7** | **8** | **9** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Frequency (f) | 2 | 5 | 6 | 10 | 8 | 5 | 3 |
**Solution**
Total = 39 (odd), so the median is the [[39 + 1/2]] = 20th value. Cumulative frequencies: 2, 7, 13, 23, … The 14th to 23rd values are all 6, so the 20th value is 6. **Median = 6 years**.
> ⚠️ **Watch out!** Always arrange data in order **before** choosing the middle value. The middle of an unsorted list is usually not the median!

pages.title: Exercise 14.2
pages.body:

5. Find the mean and median of 3, 5, 6, 7, 29. Which better describes a "typical" value? Why?

questions.q: Find the median of the shoe sizes: 6, 7, 5, 8, 7, 6, 6, 9, 7, 5. ___
Find the median number of children per family from Exercise 14.1, question 2.
The median of the numbers 4, 6, x, 10, 12 (in ascending order) is 8. Find x. If the mean of these five numbers is also 8, check that this is true.
Find the mean and median of 3, 5, 6, 7, 29. Which better describes a "typical" value? Why?

parts.a: Mean = 10, median = 6. The median is more typical, because the one large value (29) pulls the mean up.

pages.title: Chapter 14 summary
pages.body:
- Mean = sum of items ÷ number of items; for a frequency table, mean = Σfx ÷ Σf.
- Median = middle value of the ordered data (mean of the two middle values when the number of items is even).
- Cumulative frequencies help to locate the median in a frequency table.
